title: Supplement to Motion for Leave to Participate in Oral Argument

pages.text:
Via Electronic Case Filing and by First Class Mail
November 6, 2026
Hon. Scott S. Harris
Clerk of the Court
Supreme Court of the United States
1 First Street, NE
Washington, D.C. 20543
Re: Daniel Grand v. City of University Heights, Ohio et al., No. 25-695
Dear Mr. Harris:
On behalf of amicus curiae, American Planning Association (“APA”) I write this letter and ask
that it be treated as a supplement to APA’s October 29, 2026 Motion for Leave to Participate in
Oral Argument and for Divided Time (the “Motion”).  Specifically, the APA is asking for an
enlargement of time of 5 minutes for it to participate in the oral argument.
In accordance with Rule 21, counsel for both the Petitioner and for the Respondents have been
consulted. The Petitioner takes no position with respect to APA’s Motion.  The Respondents
object to APA’s Motion and do not consent to an enlargement of time.
As the APA supports neither party, an objection does not come as a surprise.  Nonetheless, the
APA respectfully submits that, if allowed, its participation in oral argument will greatly aid the
Court in rendering its decision
Sincerely,
Brian R. Smith,
Counsel of Record for American Planning Association, amicus curiae
Copy to: E. Joshua Rosenkranz, Esq., Counsel for Petitioner
               Lisa S. Blatt, Esq., Counsel for Respondents
